title: Arbitrarily large separation of uniform viscous observation time from flushing time on smooth bounded connected Euclidean domains
source_title: On uniform observability of gradient flows in the vanishing viscosity limit
author: Camille Laurent; Matthieu Léautaud
difficulty_reason: The geometric flushing condition does not itself control the small-viscosity observability time. The author constructs a smooth family with a fixed positive bottom energy, combines the weighted eigenfunction/quasimode estimates with its observation geometry, and proves a uniformly bounded exit time for the corresponding trajectories. The same family then has a growing observation lower bound, so the separation requires both the spectral construction and the explicit dynamical argument.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem1.6 only: smooth bounded connected Euclidean domain, fixed real L-infinity potential q, Dirichlet parabolic transport, internal observation on a fixed open set, and an explicit smooth family f_lambda. Full authored field construction, quasimode existence, weighted eigenfunction estimates and flushing-time proof preserved. Classical Agmon estimates are clearly stated named existing semiclassical foundations, not an omitted new local estimate. E0=n/4>0 in this construction, so no zero-energy division issue occurs. Source2.9(1)↔(2) internal observation conjugation is the only time formulation used; rescaled2.12/2.13 and boundary observation claims are not selected. The final trajectory argument is used only under its contradiction assumption of no prior exit, where the supplied directional derivative bound holds. No positive-solution equality theorem or arbitrary fixed-vector-field metric version counted.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: Explicit everywhere-escaping gradient fields combined with semiclassical eigenfunction concentration and Agmon distances show that inviscid trajectory geometry alone cannot bound uniform viscous observability time.
